$comment: Copy, fill in, and pass with --config. NOTHING user- or machine-specific belongs in the skill itself; it all lives here or in the environment.

sources.$comment: Any mix. Each emits the SAME normalized record: {title,date,summary,shared_by?,attendees?}. attendees is advisory only -- the calendar stays the attendee authority.

GENERAL MCP SOURCE, server-agnostic. A script cannot speak MCP -- the connection lives in the AGENT hosting this skill. So the agent calls whatever MCP tool it has (Otter, Fireflies, Granola, Gong...) and either exposes it as bridge_argv or drops normalized records into inbox. No data transits Fulcra.
Direct API/CLI: anything that emits normalized records on stdout.
Plain files or a directory of them.

collect.$comment: DEPRECATED shorthand for a single fulcra_files source; prefer `sources`. Kept so existing configs keep working.

detection.$comment: How a meeting-summary mail is recognised and parsed. NO note-taker is privileged in code; these defaults are vendor-neutral. Override only to support a service the defaults miss. sharer_patterns MUST contain a (?P<name>...) group; the sharer is PROVENANCE, never an attendee.

identity.$comment: self_emails are never written as contacts. internal_domains are colleagues: still worth notes, but never treated as external counterparties.

limits.$comment: max_attendees skips mass meetings (all-hands, board meetings) which are not relationship events. title_match_threshold is the token-overlap needed to join a calendar event to a summary email.

guards.$comment: Leave these true. Each was added after it corrupted real data. See references/design-notes.md.

cli.$comment: null means: use $FULCRA_CLI_COMMAND if set, else the first fulcra-api on PATH. Pin a path here only if your environment cannot express it.
